title: Primary jaw crusher, pitman bearing failure
tests: Strong, sound-ish tree except one weakness: action without interval. Forced (lubrication).
summary: The pitman bearing on a primary jaw crusher ran hot and seized after the automatic grease line to it blocked. The tree is evidenced and has a system root. One action has no interval. Tests the AI gives targeted comments.

problem.title: Pitman bearing seizure on primary jaw crusher CR-01
problem.site: Hard rock quarry, Hunter Valley NSW
problem.whatHappened: On 10 Jun 2026 the pitman bearing temperature alarm tripped CR-01 and the crusher was stopped. The rear pitman bearing was found overheated with the grease line to it blocked solid. The bearing was replaced and the shaft journal was reconditioned.
problem.where: Rear pitman bearing and its automatic grease line on CR-01.
problem.impact: Primary crushing out for 4 days, the plant ran on stockpile then stopped. Contractor machining of the journal.
problem.duty: Primary crushing of blasted rock, 600 t/h

evidence.title: Rear pitman bearing
evidence.note: Overheated, blued, rollers smeared. Journal scoring.

evidence.title: Grease line to the rear bearing
evidence.note: Line blocked with hardened grease and dirt about 1 m from the bearing. Pump delivering to the other points.

evidence.title: Lube system documentation
evidence.note: Flow switch on the rear line wired out (bypassed) 9 months earlier after nuisance alarms. Not recorded as a change.

evidence.title: Bearing temperature trend
evidence.note: Rear bearing temperature rose from 62 to 98 C in 6 hours before the trip; alarm at 90 C, trip at 100 C.

tree.text: Rear pitman bearing on CR-01 overheated and seized

children.text: Bearing ran without grease and overheated
Grease line to the rear bearing blocked with hardened grease and dirt
Flow switch on the rear line was bypassed, so a no-flow alarm could not occur
No management of change for bypassed protection; nuisance alarms were not fixed
Grease line condition and flow are not checked in the PM plan

actions.description: Replace pitman bearing, recondition journal, clear all grease lines
Reinstate the flow switch and add bypass control to the MoC procedure

task.description: Check grease flow at the end of each line and clear lines

spares.coverage: Bearing was ordered at urgent freight; shaft machined on site by contractors.

existingFields.duty: Primary crushing of blasted rock, 600 t/h
existingFields.site: Hard rock quarry, Hunter Valley NSW

problemDraft.roughNotes: cr01 rear pitman brg hot tripped. grease line to the rear bearing blocked solid, the pump was working but no grease reaching it. replaced bearing and machined the journal. 4 days. grease flow switch on that line was bypassed by someone ages ago.

draft.notes: cr01 rear pitman brg hot tripped. grease line to the rear bearing blocked solid, the pump was working but no grease reaching it. replaced bearing and machined the journal. 4 days. grease flow switch on that line was bypassed by someone ages ago.

mustSuggest.idea: Alarm response: the bearing temperature alarm gave warning but there is no action standard
Grease system design: line routing and grease type invite blockage
Check the grease type and pump pressure for the long rear line

acceptable: Nuisance alarm root cause on the flow switch
wrongOrDangerous: The electrician who bypassed it is to blame
Replace with oil lubrication as a conclusion

mustNotFlag: blame (n3 states a fact about the switch, not a person)
challenge.expectation: Mostly sound. At most 3 issues. Possibly a low point on the alarm response.
deliberateWeaknesses: a3 has no interval (no_task_interval) although craft is set
Bearing temperature alarm at 90 C gave 6 hours' warning: no response procedure noted
No condition monitoring action on the temperature trend

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Running without grease is forced deterioration: the system let a blocked line go undetected. Not normal wear.

preventive.what: Check grease delivery at the bearing end of every line and purge as needed
Bearing temperature trend review and alarm response with a time to act
Reinstate flow switches and correct the cause of nuisance alarms rather than bypass
Management of change for bypassed protection with an expiry
Hold a pitman bearing set for the crusher

capa.spares: Pitman bearing set for CR-01; 35 day lead time on a single primary crusher.
capa.rollout: All crushers and mills with automatic grease systems: check flow switches are not bypassed.

gapsToPointOut: When was it bypassed and by whom (as a record, not blame)?
